people.name: Śambhunātha
people.bio: Kaula master from Jālandhara whom Abhinavagupta names as his most admired guru; through him (and his consort as dūtī) Abhinavagupta received Kaula initiation, the Ardha-tryambaka line.

people.name: Bhūtirāja
people.bio: One of the teachers Abhinavagupta names in his own works; he taught him in the dualist/nondualist Śaiva school and was the father of two scholars.

people.name: Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa (Kashmir)
people.bio: Kashmiri Śaiva poet of the Stavacintāmaṇi, a devotional hymn to Śiva and his power on which Kṣemarāja wrote a commentary; not the dramatist of the Veṇīsaṃhāra.

people.name: Lalleshwari (Lal Ded)
people.bio: Fourteenth-century Kashmiri mystic of the Kashmir Śaiva school whose vakhs (sayings) are among the earliest poems in Kashmiri; revered by Hindus and Muslims alike and linked by tradition with Nund Rishi and the Rishi order.

people.name: Śivopādhyāya
people.bio: Late Kashmiri commentator whose commentary completes Kṣemarāja’s on the Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra in the Kashmir Series of Texts and Studies edition (1918).

people.name: Swami Manakak (Manas Ram Mongra)
people.bio: Kashmiri master recognised around 1860 who initiated Swami Ram, the root of Swami Lakshmanjoo’s modern line (Lakshmanjoo Academy).

people.name: Pandit Maheshwar Nath Razdan
people.bio: Kashmiri pandit under whom the young Lakshmanjoo studied Sanskrit and Śaiva philosophy from 1926 to 1933.

people.name: Isabelle Ratié
people.bio: French historian of Indian philosophy, Professor at the Collège de France (chair of the History of Indian Systems of Thought, 2025); her work on the Pratyabhijñā and on lost fragments of Utpaladeva’s Vivṛti includes Le Soi et l’Autre (Brill 2011) and Utpaladeva on the Power of Action (HOS 2021).

people.name: Raffaele Torella
people.bio: Italian philologist of Sapienza University of Rome; his critical edition and annotated translation of Utpaladeva’s Īśvarapratyabhijñākārikā gave the first complete text of the author’s Vṛtti, from a manuscript he found in Trivandrum.

people.name: John Nemec
people.bio: Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Virginia; his two volumes The Ubiquitous Śiva edit and translate Somānanda’s Śivadṛṣṭi, the first work of the Pratyabhijñā school.

people.name: David Peter Lawrence
people.bio: Philosopher of religion at the University of North Dakota; author of Rediscovering God with Transcendental Argument (SUNY 1999), a study of the Pratyabhijñā of Utpaladeva and Abhinavagupta.

people.name: Jürgen Hanneder
people.bio: German Indologist, Professor of Indology and Tibetology at Philipps-Universität Marburg, where he directs research on the intellectual history of Kashmir; his doctorate edited Abhinavagupta’s Mālinīślokavārttika (Abhinavagupta’s Philosophy of Revelation, 1998).

people.name: Lyne Bansat-Boudon
people.bio: French Indologist, directrice d’études émérite at the École pratique des hautes études (religious sciences); doctoral supervisor of Isabelle Ratié.

people.name: Kanti Chandra Pandey
people.bio: Lucknow scholar known for “discovering” Abhinavagupta for modern scholarship (Abhinavagupta: An Historical and Philosophical Study); he founded the Abhinavagupta Institute of Aesthetics and Śaiva Philosophy at the University of Lucknow.

people.name: Navjivan Rastogi
people.bio: Lucknow scholar of Abhinavagupta in K.C. Pandey’s line; his Krama Tantricism of Kashmir (1979) was the first study of the Krama system, followed by Introduction to the Tantrāloka (1986). Padma Shri 2024.

people.name: Raniero Gnoli
people.bio: Italian Indologist and historian of religion who taught at Rome (1964–2000) and translated Abhinavagupta’s Tantrāloka into Italian, besides many other Śaiva and Buddhist texts.

people.name: Baljinath Pandit (B. N. Pandit)
people.bio: Kashmiri Sanskrit scholar and authority on Kashmir Śaivism, professor at Himachal Pradesh University and author of History of Kashmir Śaivism (1989) and Specific Principles of Kashmir Śaivism.

people.name: Sadananda Das
people.bio: Sanskrit scholar (PhD Pune) who has taught Sanskrit and Kashmir Śaivism at Leipzig University since 2005 and co-leads Kashmir Śaiva retreat seminars with Bettina Bäumer at Deer Park Institute, Bir.

people.name: George Barselaar
people.bio: Student of Swami Lakshmanjoo who teaches the Lakshmanjoo Academy’s online study retreats with John and Denise Hughes.

people.name: Denise Hughes
people.bio: Student of Swami Lakshmanjoo whom he designated, with John Hughes, to continue publishing his teachings; teaches the Lakshmanjoo Academy’s online study retreats.

people.name: Alka Tyagi
people.bio: Delhi University professor, poet and Satyananda-trained yoga teacher who teaches Trika texts (Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam, Vijñāna Bhairava) online and in retreats through Tantravimarśa; author of Bhairava and Bhāvanā.

people.name: Gabriel Pradīpaka
people.bio: Argentine-born teacher of Trika based in Moscow; founder of Parabhairavayoga (2016) and of the Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism website. He names Muktananda as his guru and Lakshmanjoo as his Trika guru.

people.name: Swami Chetanananda (The Movement Center)
people.bio: American teacher, successor of Swami Rudrananda (Rudi) after 1973 and founder of the Nityananda Institute, now The Movement Center (Oregon); teaches eyes-open meditation and the Śiva Sūtras and chairs the Institute for Śaiva and Tantric Studies. Not the Ramakrishna monk of the same name.
